title: Hypoglycemia at the Bedside: Recognition and Reassessment
subject: Ward Protocols
preview: Hypoglycemia may produce sweating, tremor, hunger, confusion, seizure or reduced consciousness.
quickRevision: Hypoglycemia may produce sweating, tremor, hunger, confusion, seizure or reduced consciousness.
Recheck glucose and assess recurrence risk, especially with long-acting insulin or sulfonylureas.
Investigate missed meals, renal impairment, medication mismatch and acute illness after stabilizing the patient.

sections.title: Recognize the situation
points: Hypoglycemia may produce sweating, tremor, hunger, confusion, seizure or reduced consciousness.
Confirm glucose promptly and provide appropriate glucose treatment using a safe route based on consciousness and swallowing ability.

sections.title: Clinical decisions & differential
points: Recheck glucose and assess recurrence risk, especially with long-acting insulin or sulfonylureas.
Investigate missed meals, renal impairment, medication mismatch and acute illness after stabilizing the patient.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not give oral intake to a patient unable to protect their airway.

quiz.question: Which patient needs a nonoral route of glucose treatment?
options: An unconscious patient unable to swallow
A patient with normal glucose and headache
quiz.explanation: An unconscious patient unable to swallow. Do not give oral intake to a patient unable to protect their airway.
